questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs has a therapeutic role in the management of his condition?
questions.explanation: This patient has serotonin syndrome secondary to the use of multiple serotonergic drugs. Prompt initiation of cyproheptadine is recommended in the treatment of serotonin syndrome.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs can be used in the management of anxiety?
questions.explanation: Meprobamate can be used to treat anxiety. In view of its additive sedating effects, abusive potential, and lethality in overdose, it is not used frequently.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antihistamines can be used in the treatment of eating disorders?
questions.explanation: Cyproheptadine causes weight gain and can be used in patients with anorexia nervosa.

questions.question_text: Flumazenil is useful in the reversal of all of the following medication overdoses EXCEPT?
questions.explanation: Flumazenil does not reverse the effects of barbiturates or opioids.

questions.question_text: What is the most likely cause of these symptoms?
questions.explanation: Nefazodone inhibits oxidative metabolism mediated by CYP3A (metabolizes alprazolam), which could result in the increase of alprazolam level.

questions.question_text: What is the most appropriate treatment for Mr. A's new onset movement disorder?
questions.explanation: Amantadine is the preferred choice because this patient has closed-angle glaucoma and anticholinergics will worsen his medical conditions.

questions.question_text: Benzodiazepine and no benzodiazepine hypnotic drugs bind to the GABAA receptor and exert their action by which of the following mechanism?

options.text: Triggering the influx of sodium into the neuronal cell and thus causing the cell membrane to be hyperpolarized.
Increasing the affinity of GABA for its receptor site and thus enhancing the channel opening effect.
Create a conformational change in the GABA receptor such that both GABA and dopamine act as agonists.
Triggering the influx of chloride into the cell and thus creating an inhibitory effect on neuronal cells
Triggering the influx of potassium into the neuronal cell and thus causing the cell membrane to be hyperpolarized.

correct_answer.text: Triggering the influx of chloride into the cell and thus creating an inhibitory effect on neuronal cells

correct_answers.text: Triggering the influx of chloride into the cell and thus creating an inhibitory effect on neuronal cells

questions.explanation: Barbiturate, benzodiazepine, and non-benzodiazepine hypnotic drugs are positive allosteric modulators of the GABA receptor complex.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding lithium therapy during pregnancy EXCEPT?

options.text: In women with mild and infrequent episodes of illness, lithium therapy should be gradually (>2 weeks) tapered before conception
In women with severe episodes but at moderate risk for relapse in the short term, lithium therapy should be tapered before conception but reinstituted after 7 to 9 weeks
Women with severe and frequent episodes of illness, lithium should be continued throughout gestation in conjunction with counseling regarding reproductive risks
Lithium should be restarted in the second trimester in women with severe episodes and at moderate risk of relapse
Risk of Ebstein anomaly after prenatal lithium exposure rises from 1 in 20,000 to 1 in 1,000

correct_answer.text: In women with severe episodes but at moderate risk for relapse in the short term, lithium therapy should be tapered before conception but reinstituted after 7 to 9 weeks

correct_answers.text: In women with severe episodes but at moderate risk for relapse in the short term, lithium therapy should be tapered before conception but reinstituted after 7 to 9 weeks

questions.explanation: Women with severe episodes but at moderate risk for relapse in the short term should be tapered before conception but reinstituted after 7 to 9 weeks.

questions.question_text: Which of the following medications when given with clozapine has the potential to increase the risk of asterixis?
questions.explanation: Clozapine, lithium, and Carbamazepine, when administered alone and when used concurrently, increase the risk of asterixis.

questions.question_text: Ramelteon acts on melatonin receptors MT1 and MT2 that are located in which area of the brain?
questions.explanation: Ramelteon is an agonist on MT1 and MT2 receptors located in the suprachiasmatic nucleus, which regulates the sleep-wake cycle.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antihistamines acts both on histamine and serotonin receptors?
questions.explanation: Cyproheptadine acts both on histamine and serotonin receptors.

questions.question_text: What is the best choice for treating insomnia in breast-feeding women?
questions.explanation: Zolpidem may be safer in pregnant women and is a category B medication in pregnancy.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding sodium oxybate (Xyrem) EXCEPT?

options.text: Used for cataplexy in patients with narcolepsy
Food significantly enhances the bioavailability of sodium oxybate.
It is indicated in the treatment of excessive daytime sleepiness
It is a schedule III drug under the Controlled Substances Act
It is taken at bedtime and again 2.5 to 4 hours later

correct_answer.text: Food significantly enhances the bioavailability of sodium oxybate.

correct_answers.text: Food significantly enhances the bioavailability of sodium oxybate.

questions.explanation: Food significantly decreases the bioavailability of sodium oxybate, and it is recommended to take the drug on an empty stomach.

questions.question_text: To reduce the neonatal risks, it is recommended that the dose of VPA should not exceed more than
questions.explanation: Neonatal risks may be reduced by being careful not to exceed the VPA dose of 1,000 mg per day or a serum concentration of 70 g per ml.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding Lamotrigine-induced Steven-Johnson syndrome are true EXCEPT?

options.text: The risk is higher if the dosage is escalated too rapidly
Rarely it may be associated with multiple organ failure
The incidence in adults is about 0.1%
The risk is higher with concomitant phenytoin therapy.
Most cases appear after 2-8 weeks of therapy

correct_answer.text: The risk is higher with concomitant phenytoin therapy.

correct_answers.text: The risk is higher with concomitant phenytoin therapy.

questions.explanation: Adding phenytoin does not increase the risk of Lamotrigine-induced Steven-Johnson syndrome.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding carbamazepine induced hyponatremia?

options.text: It occurs in 1% of patients taking Carbamazepine
It is a likely result of Carbamazepine antidiuretic effect
It is common in male gender

correct_answer.text: It is a likely result of Carbamazepine antidiuretic effect

correct_answers.text: It is a likely result of Carbamazepine antidiuretic effect

questions.explanation: Carbamazepine-induced hyponatremia is likely a result of carbamazepine's antidiuretic effect.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs' absorption is enhanced when taken with food?
questions.explanation: Absorptions of Ziprasidone, Diazepam, Vilazodone, and Carbamazepine are enhanced when taken with food.

questions.question_text: Which of the following mood stabilizers should be avoided as a first-line agent in women of childbearing age?
questions.explanation: VPA should be avoided as a first-line agent in any women of reproductive age.

questions.question_text: Electrocardiographic (ECG) changes occur with which of the following antipsychotic drugs' therapy?
questions.explanation: All of the above antipsychotic medications can cause ECG changes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following medications should be avoided in a patient taking clozapine?
questions.explanation: Clozapine when combined with captopril, sulfonamides, propylthiouracil, or carbamazepine increases the risk of bone marrow suppression and agranulocytosis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding antipsychotic drugs?

options.text: Atypical agents increase c-fos in prefrontal cortex
Conventional agents block 75% to 90% of D2 receptors, whereas clozapine blocks only 40% to 60%
Atypical agents produce depolarization blockade both in A9 and A10 dopamine neurons
The A10 mesolimbic pathway is possibly associated with psychosis
Conventional antipsychotic agents increase c-fos in nucleus accumbens and striatum

correct_answer.text: Atypical agents produce depolarization blockade both in A9 and A10 dopamine neurons

correct_answers.text: Atypical agents produce depolarization blockade both in A9 and A10 dopamine neurons

questions.explanation: Conventional agents produce depolarization blockade both in A9 (substantia nigra) and A10 (mesolimbic) dopamine neurons, and not the atypical agents.

questions.question_text: Lithium can mitigate which of the following adverse effects of carbamazepine?
questions.explanation: Carbamazepine is known to cause leukopenia, and lithium is associated with leukocytosis. Thus, it can mitigate carbamazepine-induced leukopenia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following percentages most closely resembles the incidence of SSRI-resistant obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)?
questions.explanation: Approximately 40% of patients with OCD do not respond adequately to SSRIs and may require additional treatments.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most likely mechanism of neutropenia associated with Carbamazepine therapy?

options.text: Inhibition of colony-stimulating factor in the bone marrow
Autoimmune destruction of the bone marrow

correct_answer.text: Inhibition of colony-stimulating factor in the bone marrow

correct_answers.text: Inhibition of colony-stimulating factor in the bone marrow

questions.explanation: Neutropenia due to Carbamazepine is likely a result of its antidiuretic effect.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding nonbenzodiazepine hypnotic drugs?

options.text: Zaleplon has a rapid onset of action and short duration
Zaleplon is absorbed slowly when taken after fatty meal
Zolpidem is a selective GABAA receptor 0,-subunit agonist
Zaleplon has a half-life of >6 hours
Risk of dependence with Zolpidem increases with the duration of treatment

correct_answer.text: Zaleplon has a half-life of >6 hours

correct_answers.text: Zaleplon has a half-life of >6 hours

questions.explanation: Zaleplon has an ultra short half-life of 1 hour, not over 6 hours.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding Eszopiclone?

options.text: Unpleasant taste is a very common side effect
It is the R(-)enantiomer of Zopiclone
It is structurally related to Zaleplon

correct_answer.text: Unpleasant taste is a very common side effect

correct_answers.text: Unpleasant taste is a very common side effect

questions.explanation: Eszopiclone causes unpleasant taste, which is a very common side effect. It is not structurally related to Zaleplon.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sets of side effects is possible as a result of a drug-drug interaction (DDI) between tramadol and paroxetine?

options.text: Seizures, hyperthermia, and enhanced analgesic effect of tramadol.
Mental status changes, hypertension, and myoclonus.
Hypotension, decreased tendon reflexes, and arrhythmias.

correct_answer.text: Mental status changes, hypertension, and myoclonus.

correct_answers.text: Mental status changes, hypertension, and myoclonus.

questions.explanation: Serotonin syndrome may occur as a result of a DDI between tramadol and paroxetine because both these agents inhibit serotonin reuptake.

questions.question_text: Lithium was reported to be effective in mania by
questions.explanation: Dr. John Cade, an Australian psychiatrist, discovered the mood stabilization effects of lithium bicarbonate.

questions.question_text: A 27-year-old African American woman is brought in by the squad after an overdose with amitriptyline. ECG shows dysrhythmia. Besides supportive measures, adding which of the following is recommended first-line agent in the management of dysrhythmia induced by TCA overdose?
questions.explanation: Sodium bicarbonate is the first-line treatment for TCA-induced dysrhythmia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following actions of tricyclics is/are responsible for its toxicity during overdose?
questions.explanation: Clinical manifestations of tricyclic overdose are categorized as anticholinergic effects, cardiovascular effects, and central nervous effects. TCA toxicity is mediated by reuptake inhibition of norepinephrine and antagonism at adrenergic and cholinergic receptors.

questions.question_text: Pharmacokinetics, one of the principles that determines the clinical efficacy of a drug, is described as

options.text: Genetic differences in the absorption and degradation of drugs
Genetic differences in the behavioral response to pharmacologic agents
Genetic differences in tissue sensitivity to drug
What the body does to the drug
What the drug does to the body

correct_answer.text: What the body does to the drug

correct_answers.text: What the body does to the drug

questions.explanation: Pharmacokinetics is defined as what the body does to the drug, whereas pharmacodynamics describes what the drug does to the body.

questions.question_text: In addition to declining WBC and ANC counts, which of the following is an indication for interrupting clozapine therapy?
questions.explanation: Eosinophilia has been reported to occur with clozapine, indicating developing neutropenia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a known complication of chronic SSRI use?
questions.explanation: Chronic SSRI use is reported to be associated with short-term memory impairment, concentration problems, and sleep disturbances.

questions.question_text: As an astute clinician, you recognize the potential for an important DDI between clozapine and fluvoxamine. The DDI involves which of the following cytochrome enzymes:
questions.explanation: Fluvoxamine is a potent inhibitor of CYP1A2, and clozapine is a substrate of CYP1A2.

questions.question_text: Which of the following neurotransmitters is postulated to mediate changes in weight associated with psychotropic drugs?
questions.explanation: Antipsychotic drugs cause weight gain through their effect on serotonin, histamine, dopamine, and adrenergic receptors.

questions.question_text: All of the following are risk factors for seizure during bupropion therapy EXCEPT?

options.text: History of febrile seizures during childhood

questions.explanation: Bupropion is contraindicated in patients with a history of seizure disorder, febrile childhood seizures, head injury, CNS tumor, and eating disorder.

questions.question_text: What is the next best action for a patient experiencing adverse effects after starting Aripiprazole due to a DDI with rifampicin?

options.text: Stop Aripiprazole and start him on a different antipsychotic.

correct_answer.text: Stop Aripiprazole and start him on a different antipsychotic.

correct_answers.text: Stop Aripiprazole and start him on a different antipsychotic.

questions.explanation: Rifampicin induces CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 enzymes, decreasing the level and efficacy of Aripiprazole, necessitating a switch to a different antipsychotic.

questions.question_text: All of the following drugs are associated with hyponatremia EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Lamotrigine is not associated with hyponatremia; the others can cause it.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs has high therapeutic index?
questions.explanation: Haloperidol has a wide therapeutic index, while Lithium and Nortriptyline have narrow therapeutic indices.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true regarding psychotropic's and dialysis EXCEPT?

options.text: Hemodialysis is the best treatment for VPA overdose
Hemodialysis is indicated in overdose with venlafaxine
Mainstay treatment of lithium toxicity is hemodialysis
Drugs with low protein binding are good candidates for dialysis
Drugs with high protein binding are not cleared during dialysis

correct_answer.text: Hemodialysis is indicated in overdose with venlafaxine

correct_answers.text: Hemodialysis is indicated in overdose with venlafaxine

questions.explanation: Venlafaxine overdose is managed with gastric lavage and supportive measures; hemodialysis is not indicated.

questions.question_text: All of the following are risk factors for torsades de pointe during parenteral administration of haloperidol therapy EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Hypokalemia is a risk factor for the development of torsades de pointes but not hyperkalemia.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old woman with major depression and chronic pain is on amitriptyline, citalopram, and Zolpidem. After 2 weeks on the new drug, she develops urinary retention and her ECG shows conduction abnormalities. The second antidepressant is most likely to be which of the following?
questions.explanation: Mirtazapine is known to cause urinary retention and conduction abnormalities.

questions.question_text: All of the following are advantages of guanfacine over clonidine EXCEPT?
questions.explanation: Guanfacine is not available as a transdermal preparation; it is less sedating and has less severe withdrawal symptoms compared to clonidine.

questions.question_text: What is the prevalence of Ebstein anomaly during lithium therapy in the first trimester?
questions.explanation: The risk of Ebstein anomaly after prenatal lithium exposure rises significantly.

questions.question_text: What is the half-life of immediate-release venlafaxine?
questions.explanation: Immediate-release venlafaxine has a half-life of approximately 4 hours.

questions.question_text: Which of the following TCAs is devoid of sedative effects?
questions.explanation: Protriptyline does not cause sedation and is used in the treatment of narcolepsy.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding duloxetine = symbalta (as venlafaxine) are true EXCEPT:

options.text: The drug is mainly metabolized by the CYP3A4 P450 isozyme
The drug is potent inhibitor of neuronal serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake
The drug can affect urethral resistance
It is indicated in the treatment of fibromyalgia

correct_answer.text: The drug is mainly metabolized by the CYP3A4 P450 isozyme

correct_answers.text: The drug is mainly metabolized by the CYP3A4 P450 isozyme

questions.explanation: Duloxetine is metabolized primarily by CYP2D6 and CYP1A2.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding Selegiline transdermal patch is true?

options.text: When used in children, dietary modifications are required at any dose.
The drug is Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved for bipolar depression
No dietary restrictions are required when dosed at 6 mg per 24 hours
Orthostatic hypotension is the most common side effect with the drug

correct_answer.text: No dietary restrictions are required when dosed at 6 mg per 24 hours

correct_answers.text: No dietary restrictions are required when dosed at 6 mg per 24 hours

questions.explanation: No dietary restrictions are needed when selegiline is dosed at 6 mg per 24 hours.

questions.question_text: A 34-year-old woman comes to your office with symptoms suggestive of OCD. This new information prompts you to reconsider prescribing drug X. Which of the following agents is most likely to be drug X?
questions.explanation: Clomipramine is FDA approved in the treatment of OCD and can lower seizure threshold.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs has the greatest evidence for causing depression as an unwanted side effect?
questions.explanation: Isotretinoin has a well-documented association with depression and suicide risk.
